# Retrieval golden fixtures

`golden-public.yaml` is a small, fully synthetic retrieval golden set that
every SDK runs against its own pipeline. The paths and queries describe a
fictional organisation, so the fixture can be redistributed and
regenerated by anyone.

## Schema

```yaml
queries:
  - id: string            # stable identifier the SDK tests select by
    q: string             # the user query
    any_of: [path, ...]   # passes when any of these is in the top-K
    must_retrieve: [path] # passes when all of these are in the top-K
    notes: string         # optional, human context
```

A query declares `any_of`, `must_retrieve`, or both.

## How every SDK consumes it

1. Load `golden-public.yaml`.
2. Synthesise one chunk per expected path. Its title, summary and content
   are derived from the path slug and the originating query, so BM25 and
   semantic retrieval can both plausibly surface it.
3. Add the fixed distractor slate (holiday calendar, stationery budget,
   HR handbook, office wifi) so each query has noise to rank against.
4. Run the query through the pipeline at the mode under test (`bm25`,
   `hybrid`, `hybrid-rerank`) with `top_k: 5`.
5. Pass when the top-K contains at least one `any_of` path, or every
   `must_retrieve` path.

The Go suite lives in `go/retrieval/golden_test.go` and the Python suite
in `sdks/py/tests/test_retrieval_golden.py`.

## Adding queries

Keep every path and query synthetic. Never capture a report from a real
brain into this directory: reports embed absolute paths, article titles
and corpus statistics that belong to whoever owns that brain.
